text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementPsychologyThe Difference Between Nice and KindHow we talk about good deeds and acts of altruismKFBy Kristen French11:00 AM CST on November 10, 2026Add Nautilus to GooglePerhaps you have heard the story of the Polish Franciscan friar who volunteered to die in place of a total stranger at the Auschwitz concentration camp in 1941. When Nazi guards selected ten prisoners to starve to death in retaliation for an escape, one of those men, Franciszek Gajowniczek, cried out for his family. The friar, Maximilian Kolbe, stepped forward to take his place.Powered By 103.4K 00ShareNextStayIt is hard to imagine a more selfless act. But the concept of selflessness has long been the subject of intense debate among theologians, economists, philosophers, and biologists. English philosopher Thomas Hobbes famously argued that every human action is ultimately driven by pure self-interest: If you help someone at a cost to yourself, you do it because it relieves your own empathic distress or puffs you up with pride. Read more: “How Discovering an Equation for Altruism Cost George Price Everything”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
